findings.description: The `ticket-link` job checks out the pull request’s merge revision and runs `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` from that revision as its required validator. A contributor can change the script or workflow in their pull request to return success despite a missing issue link or backlog update, while retaining the `ticket-link` check name.
findings.title: PR authors can bypass the ticket gate

citations.citation:
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, edited]

# Read access only, on a public repository: the token can read nothing that a signed-in visitor
# cannot. GraphQL does not answer anonymous requests, so the job token is needed. Keeping the
# token away from the script would not protect it: on a `pull_request` event this workflow file
# itself comes from the pull request, so its author decides what runs with the token either
# way. GitHub's answer to that is the read-only token, which is all this job asks for. If this

jobs:
  ticket-link:
    name: ticket-link
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: A ticket PR closes its own issue and has updated the backlog
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: node scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts BACKLOG.md

9. **Required checks pass on the head commit.** Before a merge, the workflows `check.yml` and
   `ticket-link.yml` have succeeded for the pull request's head: `check` on Linux and on
   Windows, and `ticket-link`. A local `npm run check` does not replace it; the tests
   had only ever run on Windows. A red or missing check sends the pull request back to a fix.
For pull_request events, GITHUB_REF is the pull request merge branch and GITHUB_SHA is its latest merge commit.

evidence.explanation: The workflow uses `pull_request`, checks out its default ref, and executes the checked-out script; the script controls the exit code. GitHub documents that the event ref is the PR merge branch, and the repository makes this result part of its pre-merge gate.

findings.dismiss_explanation: Decided by the repository owner on Nov 13 2026. The ticket-link check is meant to catch slips, not deliberate bypass, and AGENTS.md says so. This is a single-maintainer repository where the owner reviews every pull request, including changes to the check itself. Running the validator from the base branch is noted as later hardening work.

findings.description: The new workflows define check contexts, but neither workflow configuration nor the documented process enables branch protection that requires those contexts on `main`. With the repository’s documented absence of branch protection, a pull request can be merged while either platform check or `ticket-link` is red or missing.
findings.title: Failing checks do not block merges

findings.description: The new `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` writes to `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` and sets `process.exitCode` in its entry block, which the rule reserves for `src/cli.ts`. The same pattern appears in the new `scripts/ticket-ready.ts` (its entry block writes both streams and sets `process.exitCode`), so the rule is departed from in two files. The author's notes say the human will decide whether the convention is scoped to `src/`, but the rule as written names no exception, so the code departs from it until that decision is made. Any later change to the entry block also has to be checked by hand against this rule.
findings.title: Script output and exit code are set outside src/cli.ts

citations.citation: Confine process output and exit-code mutation to src/cli.ts

evidence.explanation: Rule 4522070 says only `src/cli.ts` may access `process.stdout`, `process.stderr` and `process.exitCode`. Both new scripts access them directly from their entry blocks, and the rule has no exception for `scripts/`. The PR author disputes the rule's scope, but the literal rule is violated.

findings.dismiss_explanation: Decided by the repository owner on Nov 13 2026: the rule was amended in this pull request, not the code. AGENTS.md now scopes the convention to src/ and states that factory scripts under scripts/ touch the process only in their entry block, with every function returning values. Both scripts follow that. Qodo's copy of the rule keeps the old text until the rules are imported from main after the merge.

findings.description: The new `pr-ticket-check` tests read the repository’s live `BACKLOG.md` and assert its current T-001 and T-007 status strings rather than using a fixed fixture. A later, valid backlog cleanup changes those unrelated strings and fails `npm test`, which the new Linux and Windows check jobs both run.
findings.title: Backlog edits can break both test jobs

evidence.explanation: The tests open the live backlog and assert exact statuses already present there; `npm run check` runs the test suite in both newly added matrix jobs. The ticket-ready suite has the same fixture-coupling pattern for a historical ticket file.

findings.description: The investigation step passes `github.event.issue.body` from the `labeled` event to `ticket-ready.ts`, without checking the current issue body. If the issue is edited after labeling but before the queued job runs, the guard can approve a removed investigation or reject one added before execution, while the agent reads the current ticket.
findings.title: An edited ticket can pass on stale text

findings.description: The `ticket-link` checkout has no explicit head ref, so `run` reads `BACKLOG.md` from the pull request’s synthetic merge commit rather than the head commit specified by its input contract. If the base branch changes that row before a queued or rerun check executes, the result can reflect content absent from the submitted head or reject a head that contains the expected row.
findings.title: Ticket results can reflect the wrong tree

findings.description: The workflow treats every nonzero result from `node scripts/ticket-ready.ts` as an empty or missing Investigation section. If Node cannot load the script or the guard crashes, the step removes `ready-for-agent` and tells the human to edit the ticket instead of identifying the tooling failure.
findings.title: Guard failures blame a valid ticket

citations.citation:
// Usage: ISSUE_BODY=... node scripts/ticket-ready.ts
// Exit codes: 0 the section is there, 1 it is not.

run: |
          if node scripts/ticket-ready.ts; then
            exit 0
          fi
          # The label comes off so that adding it again is a new `labeled` event. If it stayed,
          # the corrected ticket could not be started the way the comment says.
          if gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --remove-label ready-for-agent; then
            retry="then add the \`ready-for-agent\` label again (this run removed it)."
          else
            retry="then remove the \`ready-for-agent\` label and add it again (this run could not remove it)."
          fi
          # A comment that cannot be posted must not hide what happened: the same instruction
          # goes to the job log either way, and the step still ends as a failure.
          message="Not started: this ticket has no \`**Investigation.**\` section, or the section is empty. Check its requirements and assumptions against the code (Codebase Wisdom), add the result to the issue body, $retry"
          gh issue comment "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --body "$message" \
            || echo "::warning::The comment could not be posted on issue $ISSUE_NUMBER."
          echo "::error::The agent did not start on issue $ISSUE_NUMBER. $message"
          exit 1

evidence.explanation: The script documents exit 1 for an absent section, but the shell's single `if` failure path handles all nonzero statuses by removing the label and posting the same ticket-content message.

findings.description: `FENCE_OPEN` (`^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})`) treats any line that starts with three backticks as an opening fence, even one like "```npm test``` passes". CommonMark does not count that as a fence, because a backtick fence's info string cannot contain backticks. Because the fence never closes, `visibleLines` blanks every later line, so `hasInvestigation` turns away a ticket whose Investigation section comes after such a line, even though GitHub shows it.
findings.title: A one-line triple-backtick span hides the rest of a ticket

evidence.explanation: The doc comment says an unterminated fence hides everything after it "which is how GitHub renders it". But the opening regex accepts lines that GitHub renders as inline code, so the guard gives the wrong answer (it fails closed) on bodies that render correctly.

findings.description: In `hasInvestigation`, `NEXT_SECTION` treats deeper Markdown headings and lines beginning with a bold phrase ending in a period as section boundaries, stopping before it reads their content. When `## Investigation` begins with a subheading such as `### What was checked`, or its prose begins with `**Checked.**`, the guard can return false, causing the label workflow to remove `ready-for-agent` and post a misleading rejection.
findings.title: Investigations written with sub-headings are refused

evidence.explanation: `HEADING` accepts an Investigation heading, but `NEXT_SECTION` matches headings at every level and bold phrases ending in a period at the start of a line. The content loop breaks on those matches before examining the line or text beneath a nested heading. AGENTS.md asks for what was checked, found, and changed, which can naturally appear under subheadings; when the guard returns false, the workflow takes its label-removal path.

findings.description: `checkPrTicket` treats every T-NNN in the PR title as a ticket the PR finishes, and requires the BACKLOG row for each one to say `done (PR <this number>)`. A title such as `feat(config): custom section names (T-027, split from T-008)`, written the same way as the existing T-027 backlog row, cannot pass unless the author overwrites T-008's history row `done (PR 21)`.
findings.title: Titles naming an earlier ticket stay red
